title: Efficient Learning of Structured Fermionic States under General Quadratic Evolution
authors: Erfan Amidi, Ali Asadian, Ali Hamed Moosavian
abstract: We prove that unknown pure fermionic states prepared from disjoint-branch fixed-particle-number blocks can be reconstructed after general quadratic evolution, including pair creation and annihilation. For a fixed particle cap per block, adaptive or nonadaptive single-copy Gaussian measurements yield classical input and circuit descriptions with prescribed fidelity and confidence, using polynomial resources in system size and inverse infidelity. The adaptive procedure has the sharper copy guarantee. Connected quartic correlations and a covariance-compatible commutant identify the hidden blocks; local states are recovered from fresh measurements or a predetermined bounded-degree moment table. Stable branch recovery gives valid preparation descriptions. Neither particle-number conservation nor block homogeneity is required; no lower bound on branch weights or covariance gaps is assumed. A certified variant returns a passive preparation whenever one exists within the promised family, without advance membership information. On the full Gaussian orbit of paired magic states, quartic measurements alone suffice, with an explicit bound converting observable error into state error.
summary: This paper develops theoretical protocols to reconstruct unknown pure fermionic states that evolve under general quadratic Hamiltonians. By utilizing single-copy Gaussian measurements and analyzing higher-order correlations, the authors achieve high-fidelity reconstruction guarantees. This advances the field by providing scalable, resource-bounded methods for characterizing complex quantum states in fermionic systems.
main_problem: The paper addresses the theoretical problem of reconstructing an unknown pure fermionic state that has undergone a general quadratic evolution, starting from structured, disjoint input blocks.
main_result: The authors prove that the state preparation can be reconstructed with high fidelity using polynomial resources in system size and inverse infidelity, even when the evolution involves pair creation/annihilation.
method: The reconstruction relies on adaptive or nonadaptive single-copy Gaussian measurements, analyzing measured covariance and connected quartic correlations to identify the hidden block structure and the governing Gaussian circuit.
model_or_system: The system involves fermionic states in $n$ modes, structured as a tensor product of disjoint input blocks acted upon by a general quadratic Hamiltonian, which can be passive (number-conserving) or active.
key_observables: Covariance ($\hat{\Gamma}$), connected fourth moments ($\hat{\kappa}$), and quartic observables ($B_I$) for the paired-magic orbit.
important_parameters: Fidelity ($f$), failure probability ($\delta$), system size ($n$), and particle cap ($r^\star$).
main_assumptions: The state must be preparable in the specific structured form involving disjoint input blocks and a quadratic evolution. The resource bounds are derived for worst-case scenarios.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the state structure and reconstruction routes. Figure 2 shows quartic reconstruction for paired-magic states. Figure 3 compares measured structure and full-state accuracy across different copy budgets.
paper_structure: The paper develops general theorems for reconstruction (Theorem 1) and a specialized procedure for the paired-magic orbit (Theorem 2). It details iterative algorithms (Adaptive/Nonadaptive) using spectral analysis of measured observables to recover the preparation circuit.
why_interesting: This work provides rigorous, resource-bounded protocols for quantum state tomography/characterization in fermionic systems, which is crucial for validating quantum simulation hardware or understanding quantum memory readout.
